ledger.note: 1710: peninsular Acadia becomes British. 'The siege of Port Royal took place in 1710, ending French rule in peninsular Acadia'; Francis Nicholson renamed it Annapolis Royal. The Treaty of Utrecht (1713) 'formally recognized British rule in the region'.
1749: Halifax becomes the capital. 'Edward Cornwallis arrived to establish Halifax with 13 transports on 21 June 1749'; Annapolis Royal had been the capital until then.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary survey; the peninsula's coast is natural, the isthmus of Chignecto, the Acadian settlements and the border with Massachusetts (Maine) are approximate; the Sunbury County of 1765 reached the Penobscot (page) and is not drawn.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row (the Maritimes are inside British Colonial Empire). Pages: Colony of Nova Scotia (the Nova Scotia article), Cape Breton Island, Colony of New Brunswick, Colony of Prince Edward Island (four). Not on the pages: an area, the infobox dates, the 1755 deportation date, the Massachusetts boundary, the end of Sunbury County's eastern-Maine claim (the page says in 1765 it 'included the territory of present-day New Brunswick and eastern Maine as far as the Penobscot River'; not drawn), the Chignecto contest of the 1750s (the new-france dossier has Beauséjour in 1755), the 1713 Utrecht detail. The 1784 division is three colonies in the page's words (Nova Scotia, Cape Breton, New Brunswick). The 1710 start is the conquest; the page treats Nova Scotia as old as 1605 (Port Royal, French Acadia), which belongs to new-france.
